after_removal: all layers and the broad synthesis remain represented

after_removal: 76 studies with a currently verified peer-reviewed version or verified workshop review
notes: Retains 74 formal peer-reviewed studies plus reviewed non-archival workshop papers S040 and S071; this is not an inclusion-time status reconstruction.

claim: RQ1 retains eight generated-code quality dimensions.
notes: Every dimension remains represented.

claim: Correctness remains the dominant RQ1 dimension.
notes: Correctness and Security remain first and second, respectively.

claim: The full RQ1 prevalence ordering is stable.
notes: The complete ordering changes even though the two leading dimensions remain stable.

claim: RQ1 Generation Derailment does not mainly depend on studies without verified peer review.
notes: The dimension remains, but 6/11 assignments (54.5%) disappear.

claim: RQ2 retains thirteen training-data issue headings in two groups.
notes: Every heading remains represented, and no heading loses more than half its support.

claim: The full RQ2 prevalence ordering is stable.
baseline: Distribution Imbalance first; Inadequate Diversity second; Correctness third; Low-Value Data fourth; Redundancy fifth
after_removal: Distribution Imbalance first; Correctness second; Inadequate Diversity third; Redundancy fourth; Low-Value Data fifth
notes: The leading heading is stable, but the next four change order.

claim: RQ3 retains twelve families, thirteen RQ2 sources, and eight RQ1 targets.
notes: No high-level RQ3 node disappears and no family loses strictly more than half its assignments.

claim: Correctness dominance and about-two-thirds concentration in the four leading RQ3 families remain.
notes: The same four-family set remains close to two-thirds of assignments.

claim: The exact ordering of the four leading RQ3 families is stable.
notes: The original four-family set remains, but three families tie for first.

claim: All 26 RQ3 relation subtypes retain peer-reviewed support.
after_removal: 22 relation subtypes; M12, M15, M17, and M24 lose all assignments
notes: The universal claim is pivotal rather than fully or mainly dependent: four local subtypes are individually fully dependent on S046, S108, or S073, while their broader relationship families remain.

claim: RQ3 links to Understandability and Generation Derailment do not mainly depend on studies without verified peer review.
notes: The targets remain, but lose 66.7% and 83.3% of assignments, respectively.

claim: M22 retains most of its supporting assignments.
notes: S081 and S105 are removed; S037 supplies the remaining peer-reviewed assignment.

claim: RQ4's five high-level comparison families remain represented.
baseline: 13 detailed detection leaves across generated-code and training-data figures
after_removal: 12/13 leaves; all five comparison families remain
notes: Generated-code detection retains 6/6 leaves and training-data detection retains 6/7; one generated-code leaf and two training-data leaves lose a strict majority of cited support.

claim: Training-data Execution-Based Validation has peer-reviewed support.
notes: This operational leaf disappears even though the broader execution/resource comparison family remains through generated-code studies.

claim: RQ5's six high-level comparison families and lifecycle branches remain represented.
baseline: 19 detailed mitigation leaves across generated-code and training-data figures
after_removal: 16/19 leaves; all six comparison families remain
notes: Eight of nineteen mitigation leaves lose a strict majority of cited support, including three that lose all support; training-data mitigation retains 19/63 leaf assignments and 11/27 cited studies.

claim: RQ5 mitigation evidence breadth does not mainly depend on studies without verified peer review.
notes: Overall assignments fall by 57.6%; training-data mitigation falls from 63 to 19 assignments and from 27 to 11 cited studies.

claim: All detailed RQ5 operational leaves have peer-reviewed support.
after_removal: 16 leaves; three lose all cited studies
notes: The universal claim is pivotal rather than fully or mainly dependent: Privacy-Preserving Input Transformation, Execution-Feedback-Based Filtering, and Curated-Source Expansion are individually fully dependent and disappear from the source lists.

claim: The existing one-exemplar crosswalk alone supports all eight generated-code headings after peer-review filtering.

notes: This filters one selected exemplar per heading and is not a search for replacement evidence.

claim: The existing one-exemplar crosswalk alone supports all thirteen training-data headings after peer-review filtering.
after_removal: 6/13 headings; seven selected exemplars are removed
notes: Seven of thirteen rows lose a detection or mitigation exemplar; this table is not an exhaustive technique-by-heading matrix.

claim: Peer-reviewed replacement evidence exists for every crosswalk heading whose selected exemplar is removed.
baseline: Current crosswalk filter retains 5/8 generated-code and 6/13 training-data headings
after_removal: Targeted full-text re-audit restores direct detection and mitigation exemplars for 8/8 and 13/13 headings
notes: The replacements establish narrow existence only; their scope limits remain and they do not establish complete subtype coverage or comparative effectiveness.

claim: The cross-RQ conclusion that quality assurance spans data, model, generation, and validation layers remains supported.
baseline: multi-layer synthesis across the full corpus
after_removal: all high-level taxonomies and lifecycle layers remain, with narrower fine-grained support
notes: The peer-reviewed subset does not support saying that every ranking, subtype, example, or technique leaf is unchanged.
